alternatives.concept: Study biological mechanisms relevant to animal health through cell biology, biochemistry, physiology, infection and immunity, pharmacology, disease mechanisms, comparative neurobiology, evolution and epidemiological research. Human-focused biomedical courses are used only for transferable mechanisms and are not presented as veterinary anatomy, diagnosis or clinical care.

alternatives.labelRationale: The completed curriculum combines comparative and general life science, human biomedical mechanisms, infection, animal-relevant neurobiology, ecology and quantitative research; the label states related animal-health science without claiming veterinary medicine.

alternatives.concept: Connect infection and immunity, epidemiology, animal-relevant neurobiology and molecular disease science with biodiversity, evolution, ecosystems, conservation, sustainable livestock farming, climate pressures, ethics and environmental governance. This route studies human-animal-environment health relationships without claiming veterinary clinical training.
basisLabels: Comparative organismal, cellular, molecular and physiological foundations relevant to animal bodies and health

alternatives.labelRationale: Four biomedical/mathematical courses are replaced by conservation, marine ecology, climate and sustainability-governance study, producing a clear One Health and welfare emphasis while retaining infection, disease and research foundations.
alternatives.distinctnessRationale: Four courses / 30 EC differ in each direction. Mathematical Methods, Molecular Cell Biology, Pharmacology and Probability & Statistics are replaced by Conservation Biology, Marine Biology, Climate Change and Governance of Sustainability. The change shifts curricular priority from biomedical mechanisms and quantitative disease science to ecosystem pressures, conservation and governance within One Health; it is not a cosmetic threshold substitution.

progressionAssessment.rationale: The schedule contains 24 unique courses / 180 EC, four courses per semester, PPD in Year 1 and seven level-300 courses. Every formal prerequisite occurs earlier and every course is available in its assigned Fall-2026-start term. Life-science foundations precede cell biology, physiology, biochemistry, laboratory work and advanced biomedical study; the brain-and-behaviour gateway precedes the research seminar; Mathematical Methods precedes Probability & Statistics.

alternativeSelection.assessment: Two complete related-field programmes pass the evidence, course-content, schedule and 30-EC distinctness gates. A third clinical veterinary route is not defensible because the workbook lacks veterinary anatomy and physiology, species-specific pathology, clinical examination and diagnostic training, animal nutrition and reproduction sequences, anaesthesia, surgery, clinical placements and veterinary capstone work. Human biomedical courses are not relabelled as those missing veterinary components.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Both address cellular and molecular foundations; UCR remains general life science rather than veterinary biology.
Both address physiological mechanisms, but UCR is explicitly human-focused and does not reproduce veterinary physiology.
Both address metabolism; UCR supplies general biochemistry rather than the integrated veterinary block.
Both include blood-related biological investigation; UCR adds molecular and microbiological laboratory methods without claiming veterinary haematology.
Both address mechanisms spanning tissues or organs; UCR is human molecular pathology and genetics rather than veterinary pathology.
Both address neurology and sensory systems; UCR uses comparative animal neurobiology but does not include veterinary anaesthesia.
The external organism-to-tissue veterinary block remains visible; no UCR course is treated as animal anatomy or histology.
The second cell-to-tissue veterinary block remains visible without duplicating UCR courses.
The veterinary circulation and respiration block remains visible; human physiology is aligned once only.
The first veterinary digestion block has no separate UCR counterpart.
The veterinary renal and urinary block has no separate UCR counterpart.
The second veterinary digestion block has no separate UCR counterpart.
The veterinary skin and derivatives block has no UCR counterpart.
UCR does not offer a veterinary reproduction sequence.
UCR does not offer species-specific locomotor anatomy and clinical study.
UCR does not offer veterinary surgery.
Both directly study infection and immune defence; the UCR course explicitly includes threats to animals as well as humans and plants.
Both address population health and disease prevention; UCR supplies general epidemiology and public health rather than veterinary public-health practice.
UCR statistical and experimental methods support the epidemiological component, but not the external economics or veterinary application.
Both connect genomes with populations; UCR emphasises evolutionary mechanisms across species rather than veterinary population genetics.
Sustainable Farming addresses livestock systems and environmental effects, complementing the external animal adaptation and welfare block without replacing it.
The dedicated veterinary nutrition component remains visible; sustainable farming is not treated as animal nutrition.
Both support professional formation; UCR PPD is general personal, civic and academic development rather than veterinary professional training.
UCR has no veterinary clinician skills line.
UCR has no second-year veterinary clinician skills line.
UCR has no second-year veterinary professional line.
The genuine 15-EC external profiling space is preserved without invented content.
UCR has no third-year veterinary clinician skills line.
The professional line including the thesis remains explicit; UCR optional independent research is comparison-only.
The genuine 7.5-EC external profiling space is preserved without invented content.

notes.text: The UCR alternatives combine comparative and general biology, human biomedical mechanisms, infection and immunity, epidemiology, animal-relevant neurobiology, ecology, welfare ethics and One Health. They do not reproduce veterinary anatomy, species-specific pathology, clinical examination, diagnostics, animal nutrition and reproduction, anaesthesia, surgery, clinical skills or veterinary placements, and therefore represent related scientific routes rather than a Veterinary Medicine curriculum.
